payload.pattern: A Next.js page gate does not cover the Server Actions declared beside it
payload.solution: A 'use server' function compiles to a stable, directly-invocable POST endpoint, so requireAdmin() in the page component protects only the render. CANON S246 found 31 unguarded actions this way, including an admin gate missing its null-guards while driving a service-role (RLS-bypassing) client. Fix: one fail-closed isAdminUser() plus per-call-shape wrappers (requireAdmin pages / requireAdminAction actions / requireAdminApi route handlers returning NextResponse, since requireAdmin throws NEXT_REDIRECT and yields a 307 in route handlers). Enforce with a static guard. Second-order and more portable: surface-guard-coverage.mjs asks per reachable surface whether a guard exists AND whether doctor actually invokes it — its first run found two guards that had shipped and were never run, reading as coverage while providing none.

payload.pattern: HttpOnly is a confidentiality flag, not an integrity one — a cookie is never an identity
payload.context: Next.js App Router + any framework that hands an identity between two server routes via a cookie. Found live in CANON S247: /auth/callback verified an Obelisk session server-to-server at the IdP, then handed the result to /api/auth/obelisk-bridge as two PLAINTEXT cookies (obelisk_identity, obelisk_email) marked HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax. The bridge read obelisk_email and minted a full Supabase session for whatever address it contained. HttpOnly stops page JavaScript from READING a cookie; it does nothing to stop anyone from SENDING one, because cookies are ordinary request headers. `curl -b 'obelisk_email=victim@example.com' /api/auth/obelisk-bridge` was a credential-free takeover of ANY account by email address, plus silent account creation for any address that did not yet exist. It shipped, passed review, and survived three prior dedicated security sessions — because the flags made it LOOK protected.
payload.solution: 1) Sign the handoff. HMAC-SHA256 over a base64url payload {sub, email, iat, exp}; verify with timingSafeEqual; refuse the legacy plaintext cookies OUTRIGHT rather than accepting them as a fallback (a fallback preserves the hole exactly). 2) Derive the key rather than inventing a required env var: HKDF-SHA256 from a secret the route already requires (e.g. the service-role key) with a domain-separating info string, preferring an explicit OBELISK_BRIDGE_SECRET when set. This ships the fix without adding a deployment prerequisite that would take login down until someone set it. Fail closed when neither exists. 3) Ship a static guard for the CLASS, not the instance: flag any route that reads an identity-shaped cookie name (email|identity|user|uid|account|principal|actor|role) without a verification primitive (HMAC / timingSafeEqual / jwtVerify / auth.getUser) in the same file. Match constant-form reads too, so moving the name into a const does not dodge it. Reference implementation: canon scripts/cookie-identity-guard.mjs + apps/web/lib/obelisk-identity-cookie.mjs.
payload.why_it_generalizes: Every prior guard in the CANON fleet reasons about WHO THE CALLER IS once resolved (admin gates, IDOR guards, RLS guards). None asked the prior question: was the resolution itself trustworthy? Any repo with a multi-step auth handoff has this blind spot.

payload.pattern: Guard-coverage census: prove every reachable surface has a BLOCKING guard, and that a page gate does not cover the Server Actions beside it
payload.context: CANON S246/S247. Two compounding blind spots in Next.js App Router repos. (a) Server Actions are directly-invocable POST endpoints. A page's requireAdmin() gate does NOT cover the 'use server' actions declared in the same file — 31 actions had zero automated coverage, and six hand-rolled ADMIN_EMAIL comparisons opened on undefined===undefined when the env var was unset. (b) More importantly, the queue that decides what to audit measures the QUEUE's coverage, not the codebase's. Both sessions found real defects only after abandoning the queue and doing a fresh live read of a surface nobody had examined.
payload.solution: Ship a census script that derives endpoint counts from LIVE SOURCE per surface (API routes, Server Actions, edge functions, Postgres RPCs, workers) and reports, for each, whether a guard exists AND whether the doctor actually RUNS it. Two things it catches that no queue contained: (1) orphaned guards — scripts that existed but were never invoked, so they read as coverage and provided none (a live observability lie); (2) surfaces with zero blocking coverage. Then make the census itself blocking. Second lesson from S247: when a guard's own fixture uses the pattern name in a COMMENT, a regex-based guard passes on prose — strip comments (preserving string literals, since the gate often lives inside one) before matching any posture. Third: never `import` a helper from an executable guard script without an `invokedDirectly` check — the module's process.exit() terminates the test file mid-run and reports a green with one test executed. Reference: canon scripts/surface-guard-coverage.mjs, scripts/server-action-authz-guard.mjs, scripts/api-route-authz-guard.mjs.
payload.why_it_generalizes: Any sibling Next.js App Router project has (a) verbatim. Every repo with lint-style guards has the prose-satisfies-the-guard and importing-an-exiting-script failure modes.

payload.pattern: A status taxonomy must be a PARTITION, or a real state goes unnamed
payload.context: studio-ops S261. Six doctor probes emitted `pass:true + warn:true` — a legitimate 'succeeded but flagged something' idiom. It matched NO predicate: isGreen excludes it (warn), isWarning excludes it (pass). Summing the four predicates classified 157 of 163 checks. The board still reconciled, because the passing tally was computed from raw `r.pass` and silently absorbed the six — so their advisories reached no human surface for as long as the idiom existed.
payload.solution: If your project renders any pass/warn/fail board: (1) enumerate the states as a partition and assert it sums to the total; (2) derive EVERY tally from that partition, never from ad-hoc boolean arithmetic over the raw fields; (3) name the succeeded-with-advisory state explicitly so it can be reported without reddening or yellowing the board. Reference implementation: scripts/lib/doctor-predicates.mjs (isAdvisoryPass, partitionCounts, assertPartition).

payload.pattern: A detector without a producer fix is a report refresh — recurrence is the proof
payload.context: studio-ops S261. A probe was built at S240 BECAUSE the nightly cloud routine wrote invalid JSON escapes into an audit sidecar on 2026-07-16. The identical corruption arrived again on 2026-08-01. The detector fired correctly both times and nothing ever changed what produced it.
payload.solution: When a defect RECURS after you shipped a detector for it, the loop is not closed — change the generator. Where the producer is a cloud routine, put its behavioural contract in a version-controlled repo file the prompt points at (server-side prompts are size-capped and invisible in diffs), so the next correction is a normal commit. Auto-repair only corruption classes with ONE unambiguous reading; refuse structural damage rather than guess, because guessing fabricates content. Our repair's refusal is what exposed that the DETECTOR itself was miscounting.
